title: Mahipal vs Rajesh Kumar @ Polia on 5 December, 2019
judges_list: Bench: Hrishikesh Roy, Dhananjaya Y Chandrachud
acts_list: Section 302 of the Penal Code. Several bail applications filed by the accused were dismissed by the Additional
Section 161 of the CrPC of the appellant and Aashish were recorded. A charge-sheet was filed against the five accused on
Section 439 of the CrPC to grant bail. The power to grant bail under Section
Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure
conclusion_clean: bail does not furnish the reasons that inform the decision, there is a presumption of the non-application of mind which may require the intervention of this Court. Where an earlier application for bail has been rejected, there is a higher burden on the appellate court to furnish specific reasons as to why bail should be granted

sections_structured.act: the Penal Code. Several bail applications filed by the accused were dismissed by the Additional

plain_summary: The High Court's order enlarging the accused on bail is set aside due to failure to consider material facts and lack of recorded reasons for granting bail.
key_reasons: The court failed to consider material facts
Order did not record reasons for granting bail
